title: Simulacro 33 — Progressive Delivery: Flagger y Argo Rollouts
focus: Progressive delivery patterns modernos: Flagger (con Istio/Linkerd/NGINX), Argo Rollouts (con service mesh o Ingress), automated canary analysis basado en métricas, Kayenta (Netflix), integración con Prometheus para promotions metrics-driven, differences entre Flagger y Argo Rollouts.

questions.scenario: Tu compañero senior dice: 'necesitamos hacer progressive delivery en el nuevo servicio'. Nunca has oído el término. Preguntas '¿es lo mismo que CI/CD?'.
questions.question: ¿Qué es progressive delivery y en qué difiere de CI/CD?

options.text: Progressive delivery es la EVOLUCIÓN de continuous delivery donde el rollout es GRADUAL y automatizado con analysis de métricas. CI/CD termina en 'deployed to production'; progressive delivery añade: canary automatizado, analysis de metrics (comparar new vs old), automatic promotion o rollback basado en criterios objetivos. James Governor (RedMonk) acuñó el término en 2018.
options.why: Correcto. CI/CD es 'llegar a producción'; progressive delivery es 'llegar a producción de forma SEGURA a scale'. Adds automated canary analysis (Kayenta, Flagger, Argo Rollouts) para decidir promotion sin human eyes. Es CD2 + observability + statistical analysis.

options.text: Progressive delivery es solo un nombre nuevo para blue/green.
options.why: Falso. Blue/green es cutover instantáneo. Progressive delivery es gradual + analyzed. Distintos conceptos.

options.text: Es específico de Kubernetes.
options.why: Falso. Aunque Kubernetes ecosystem (Argo, Flagger) es donde más se implementa, el concepto aplica a cualquier plataforma. Netflix Spinnaker para EC2/AWS también hace progressive delivery.

options.text: Progressive delivery requiere abandonar CI/CD.
options.why: Al contrario — progressive delivery se BUILDS ON TOP de CI/CD. Sin CI/CD maduro, progressive delivery no es viable.

questions.explanation: Progressive delivery pillars: (1) FEATURE FLAGS — decouple deploy de release; (2) PROGRESSIVE ROLLOUT — canary o gradual exposure; (3) OBSERVABILITY — metrics para saber qué está pasando; (4) EXPERIMENTATION — A/B testing capabilities; (5) AUTOMATED ANALYSIS — decisions sin human. Herramientas: Argo Rollouts, Flagger, Spinnaker + Kayenta (infra); LaunchDarkly, Split, Unleash (feature flags); Prometheus, Datadog (metrics). Anti-patrón común: 'tenemos Argo Rollouts' pero sin analysisTemplate configurado = solo pausa manual = no es progressive delivery real, es canary manual con más pasos.
questions.realWorld: James Governor (RedMonk) 2018 acuñó el término. Weaveworks (creators of Flagger) promueve concepto. Netflix pioneered con Spinnaker + Kayenta. Airbnb, Uber, Ticketmaster todos hacen progressive delivery. Google Cloud Deploy tiene progressive delivery features. AWS CodeDeploy tiene canary deployments (limited progressive).

questions.scenario: Instalas Argo Rollouts en tu cluster K8s. Ves que crea nuevo CRD llamado Rollout. Un colega pregunta '¿por qué no usar solo Deployments de K8s?'.
questions.question: ¿Qué es Argo Rollouts y por qué existe?

options.text: Argo Rollouts es un controller de K8s que reemplaza el Deployment nativo con un CRD 'Rollout' con capabilities avanzadas: canary con weight-based traffic splitting (via Ingress/Service Mesh), blue/green nativo, analysis templates (Prometheus queries) para automated promotion/rollback, integration con AnalysisRun. K8s Deployment solo hace rolling update básico — no canary con weights, no analysis, no blue/green nativo.
options.why: Correcto. K8s Deployment tiene 2 strategies: RollingUpdate y Recreate. Ninguna es canary real ni blue/green real. Argo Rollouts extiende K8s con progressive delivery primitives. Parte de Argo CD ecosystem (Argoproj).

options.text: Argo Rollouts es un CI/CD tool que reemplaza Jenkins.
options.why: Falso. Argo Rollouts hace deployment strategies, no CI (build/test). Argo Workflows es el CI equivalent en Argo family.

options.text: Argo Rollouts es un service mesh.
options.why: Falso. Argo Rollouts USA service meshes (Istio, Linkerd) para traffic control. No es un mesh en sí.

options.text: Argo Rollouts requiere Istio obligatoriamente.
options.why: Falso. Soporta Istio, Linkerd, Envoy AWS ALB, NGINX Ingress, SMI (Service Mesh Interface), o replica-based rollout sin traffic mesh.

questions.explanation: Argo Rollouts CRD Rollout ejemplo: strategy.canary.steps: [{setWeight: 10}, {pause: {duration: 30m}}, {setWeight: 25}, {analysis: {templates: [{templateName: success-rate}]}}]. analysisTemplate define Prometheus queries — successful = promote, fail = rollback. Trafficrouting: {istio: {virtualService: {name: my-vs}}} o {alb: {ingress: my-ingress}}. Rollout gestiona 2 ReplicaSets (canary + stable) y controla weight en el traffic router. Kubectl argo rollouts plugin permite: promote (avanzar step), abort (rollback), pause, resume. Integración con Argo CD para GitOps completo.
questions.realWorld: Argo Rollouts nació en Intuit (open sourced 2019). Ahora parte de Argoproj CNCF. Usado por Adobe, IBM, Airbnb, GoDaddy. Muy popular en K8s ecosystem porque es K8s-native (CRDs). Argo family = Argo CD (GitOps), Argo Workflows (CI), Argo Rollouts (progressive delivery), Argo Events (event-driven).

questions.scenario: Tu equipo usa Flux (GitOps de Weaveworks). Quieren añadir progressive delivery. Flagger es mencionado como opción natural.
questions.question: ¿Qué es Flagger y cómo se diferencia de Argo Rollouts?

options.text: Flagger es un operator K8s de Weaveworks (ahora CNCF sandbox) que orquesta progressive delivery. USA los K8s Deployment nativos (no reemplaza) — Flagger crea un Canary CRD que refleja el Deployment y orquesta el rollout con weighted traffic (Istio, Linkerd, App Mesh, NGINX, Gloo, etc.).
options.why: Correcto. Flagger es MÁS opinionated que Argo Rollouts. Diseñado para integrar con Flux GitOps. No reemplaza Deployments — orquesta encima de ellos.

options.text: Flagger tiene análisis automatizado de canary con múltiples metric providers built-in: Prometheus, Datadog, New Relic, Amazon CloudWatch, InfluxDB, Google Cloud Monitoring, Graphite, Dynatrace, custom webhooks.
options.why: Correcto. Metric providers ecosystem amplio. Cada progression step corre queries y decide promote basado en thresholds. Similar a Argo Rollouts analysisTemplate pero más integrado por defecto.

options.text: Argo Rollouts vs Flagger: (1) Argo reemplaza Deployment con Rollout CRD; Flagger deja Deployment intacto y añade Canary CRD encima; (2) Argo tiene primer-class integration con Argo CD; Flagger diseñado para Flux; (3) Ambos soportan mismas mesh/ingress backends; (4) Argo tiene más ecosystem community; Flagger es más simple/opinionated.
options.why: Correcto. Ambas herramientas hacen cosas similares pero con approaches distintos. La elección típicamente sigue la GitOps tool (Argo CD → Argo Rollouts; Flux → Flagger).

options.text: Flagger soporta canary, A/B testing (header-based) y blue/green con traffic mirroring.
options.why: Correcto. Flagger tiene 3 strategies: canary (weight-based), a/b (header-based), blue/green (con mirror opcional). Argo Rollouts tiene canary y blue/green pero header-based routing es más manual.

options.text: Flagger requiere Weaveworks account.
options.why: Falso. Es open source, standalone. Puedes usarlo sin Weave Cloud.

questions.explanation: Flagger arquitectura: (1) creas Canary CRD referencing el Deployment; (2) Flagger crea 'canary' Deployment como copy; (3) durante rollout, Flagger scales canary up + ajusta VirtualService weights; (4) en cada step, corre queries a metric provider; (5) if metrics pass, next step; if fail, rollback (scale canary down, weight back to 0); (6) if final step passes, promote (primary Deployment updated a nueva version). YAML declarative — configuras Canary CRD una vez, changes al Deployment triggerean automatic rollouts. Best fit: environments con Flux + Istio/Linkerd + Prometheus donde quieres progressive delivery declarative con minimum config.
questions.realWorld: Flagger creado por Weaveworks (Alexis Richardson, Stefan Prodan). Ahora Weaveworks acquired por CNCF/Progress. Usado por: Trend Micro, Twilio, WooCommerce, Uwatch, muchos con Istio+Flux stacks. Flagger fabric usa Prometheus queries built-in para SLI-based analysis.

questions.scenario: Argo Rollouts corre canary. Cada step evalúa 'success rate > 99%'. Compañero pregunta: '¿esto es realmente análisis? Es solo threshold. Netflix tiene algo llamado Kayenta que es más sophisticated'.
questions.question: ¿Qué es Kayenta y cómo mejora el analysis vs thresholds simples?

options.text: Kayenta (Netflix, OSS) es motor de automated canary analysis. En vez de thresholds fijos ('error < 1%'), compara STATISTICAMENTE distribuciones de métricas entre canary y baseline (v1 running en paralelo) usando Mann-Whitney U test. Produce score 0-100. Ventajas vs thresholds: (1) accounts for baseline variability (si v1 normalmente tiene 0.5% error, un canary con 0.6% no es problema); (2) usa datos apples-to-apples (mismo momento, misma carga, misma infra); (3) statistical significance evita false positives; (4) configurable per-metric weight y sensitivity.
options.why: Correcto. Kayenta es el estado-del-arte en canary analysis. Concepto clave: compara con BASELINE running en paralelo, no con historical data. Elimina bias de time-of-day, day-of-week, external events. Integrable con Spinnaker (Netflix's deployment tool) o standalone.

options.text: Kayenta es una herramienta de A/B testing que reemplaza Optimizely.
options.why: Falso. Kayenta es específicamente para canary analysis (infra/technical metrics), no A/B testing (business metrics).

options.text: Kayenta es feature flag tool que reemplaza LaunchDarkly.
options.why: Falso. Kayenta no gestiona flags; hace analysis de métricas post-deploy.

options.text: Kayenta solo funciona con Spinnaker de Netflix.
options.why: Kayenta puede ser standalone service (REST API). Aunque hoy la integración más común es con Spinnaker, es tool independiente.

questions.explanation: Kayenta canary judge: (1) config define 'canary config' con list de metrics + weights + sensitivity; (2) durante canary, Kayenta consulta metric source (Prometheus, Datadog, Stackdriver, etc.) para datos de canary y baseline; (3) para cada metric, Mann-Whitney U test compara distribuciones; (4) score aggregate con weights; (5) si score > threshold (ej. 75/100), promote; else abort. Ventajas vs threshold-based: (a) accepts intrinsic noise en baselines; (b) detects subtle regressions que threshold miss; (c) less false positives. Desventajas: (a) requires baseline running paralelo (extra infra); (b) complexity de config; (c) requires enough data (canaries duración muy corta = poco data = poor statistical power). Blog Netflix 2017 explica origins.
questions.realWorld: Netflix Kayenta paper y OSS. Integration con Spinnaker (default en Netflix). Google Cloud lanzó service similar. Adopters: Waze, Salesforce, Home Depot. Argo Rollouts + AnalysisTemplate puede replicar Kayenta patterns pero requires custom code. Flagger tiene extension para Kayenta backend.

questions.scenario: Configuras AnalysisTemplate en Argo Rollouts que dice 'success rate > 95%'. Necesitas escribir la PromQL query. ¿Cómo la construyes?
questions.question: ¿Qué patterns de Prometheus queries usar para canary analysis?

options.text: Success rate por servicio (5min window): sum(rate(http_requests_total{service='my-svc',code!~'5..'}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{service='my-svc'}[5m])). Comparar canary vs stable subset.
options.why: Correcto. Ratio de non-5xx requests. Rate en 5min window smooth spikes. Umbrella queries pattern. Argo Rollouts / Flagger docs muestran variantes similares.

options.text: P99 latency: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{service='my-svc'}[5m])) by (le)). Compara canary p99 vs stable p99 — canary no debe ser >1.5x peor.
options.why: Correcto. Percentiles importante — mean ok pero tail latency degraded = user experience bad. Requires histogram metrics (buckets) instrumented.

options.text: Resource usage: rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{pod=~'canary-.*'}[5m]) vs stable pods. Detecta memory leaks o CPU regressions.
options.why: Correcto. Nueva version puede tener 2x CPU usage por bad code — detectable antes de que cause outage. cAdvisor metrics via kube-state-metrics.

options.text: Custom business metrics: rate(orders_completed_total{version='canary'}[5m]) vs stable. Si canary genera menos orders, business regression aunque tech metrics ok.
options.why: Correcto. Business metrics catches bugs invisible en tech metrics (broken checkout button = 200 responses pero 0 orders). Requires app-level instrumentation.

options.text: Simple counter total sin normalización.
options.why: Antipatrón. 'canary tiene menos errors totales' no dice nada — canary tiene menos traffic también. Siempre rate/ratio, no absolute counters.

questions.explanation: Query patterns para canary analysis: (1) Success rate — ratio de good vs total; (2) Latency percentiles — histogram_quantile; (3) Saturation — CPU/memory usage; (4) Business KPIs — domain-specific counters. Argo Rollouts AnalysisTemplate config: provider: prometheus, address: http://prometheus:9090, query: '<PromQL>', successCondition: 'result[0] > 0.95', failureCondition: 'result[0] < 0.90'. Flagger similar con metricTemplates. Both support: (a) multiple metrics con AND/OR; (b) interval-based repeated checks; (c) failureLimit (# failed checks antes rollback). Best practices: (a) short intervals (30s-2min) para detección temprana; (b) failureLimit >1 para tolerar transient spikes; (c) reference baseline metric (compare canary vs stable no absolute threshold).
questions.realWorld: Argo Rollouts docs incluyen ejemplos de PromQL queries. Flagger's SLO recording rules pattern. Google Cloud Managed Service for Prometheus. Datadog similar con their query language. Adopters: Adobe (Argo), Twilio (Flagger), Airbnb custom. Best practices publicados por Weaveworks, Intuit.

questions.scenario: Configurando Argo Rollouts steps para primer canary. Opciones: [{setWeight: 10}, {pause: 5m}, {setWeight: 100}] vs [{setWeight: 5}, {analysis: 30m}, {setWeight: 25}, {analysis: 1h}, {setWeight: 50}, {analysis: 1h}, {setWeight: 100}].
questions.question: ¿Cómo elegir la granularidad de steps?

options.text: Depende del RISK PROFILE del servicio. Servicios high-traffic con SLO estricto: steps más pequeños (1%, 5%, 25%, 50%, 100%) con analysis long (1h+) para statistical power. Servicios low-risk/low-traffic: fewer steps más grandes (10%, 50%, 100%) con analysis shorter (10min). Regla: cada step = observable time para catch problems + gradually increasing blast radius.
options.why: Correcto. No hay universal correct. High-risk services (payments, auth) merecen conservative steps. Low-risk (marketing site) puede ser fast. Duration tradeoff: too short = poco data para analysis = false positives o miss bugs; too long = deploys tardan horas = friction.

options.text: Siempre usar 10 steps de 10% cada uno.
options.why: Rigid. 10 steps con analysis de 1h cada uno = 10h de deploy. Excesivo para most services.

options.text: 1 step al 50% es suficiente para detectar problemas.
options.why: 50% traffic con bug = 50% users affected. Blast radius grande. Small steps first (1-10%) es standard.

options.text: Sin analysis, solo pauses — human decides.
options.why: Elimina automation. Human at 3AM = poor decisions. Automated analysis diseñado para 24/7 objectivity.

questions.explanation: Step design ejemplos: (1) High-risk service (payment): [{weight:1, analysis:15m}, {weight:5, analysis:1h}, {weight:25, analysis:2h}, {weight:50, analysis:4h}, {weight:100}]. Total ~8h; (2) Standard service: [{weight:10, analysis:30m}, {weight:50, analysis:1h}, {weight:100}]. Total ~1.5h; (3) Low-risk (staging/internal): [{weight:50, pause:10m}, {weight:100}]. Total ~15min. Consideraciones: (a) traffic volume — low-traffic services need longer windows para statistical significance; (b) SLO — stricter SLO = smaller steps; (c) team maturity — mature teams tolerate faster deploys; (d) business hours — deploys often nocturnos o business hours dependiendo strategy. Anti-patrón: all services con mismos steps default — customize per service class.
questions.realWorld: Netflix uses different canary configs per service tier (critical vs standard vs experimental). Amazon similar. Argo Rollouts docs muestran example configs. Flagger has best-practice examples. Intuit publicó experiencias con Argo Rollouts at scale.

questions.scenario: Argo Rollouts + Istio. Rollout progression cambia weight de 10% → 25% → 50% → 100%. ¿Qué está pasando bajo el capó con Istio?
questions.question: ¿Cómo Argo Rollouts coordina con Istio para traffic splitting?

options.text: Rollout CRD tiene trafficRouting.istio.virtualService: name of pre-existing VirtualService. Argo Rollouts controller MUTA los weights en el VirtualService cada step: destinations[0].weight = 100 - canary_weight (stable), destinations[1].weight = canary_weight.
options.why: Correcto. Argo Rollouts modifica el VirtualService object en el K8s API. Istio control plane (istiod) detecta el cambio, updates Envoy sidecar configs, traffic split happens en data plane (pods).

options.text: DestinationRule required: define subsets (stable, canary) por labels. Argo Rollouts crea 2 ReplicaSets con labels distintos que corresponden a los subsets.
options.why: Correcto. DestinationRule tells Istio how to differentiate stable vs canary pods. Subsets referenciados desde VirtualService weights.

options.text: Sin sidecar (Envoy) en cada pod, no funciona. Istio requires mesh instrumentation.
options.why: Correcto. Envoy sidecar aplica los weights. Sin mesh sidecar en pods, traffic no puede ser split declarative — cae a round-robin básico de K8s Service.

options.text: Ambos ReplicaSets (canary y stable) tienen mismo Service, differ en labels. VirtualService referencia el Service, con weight routing a subsets basados en labels.
options.why: Correcto. Un Service, DestinationRule define subsets, VirtualService controla split. Pattern estándar Istio.

options.text: Argo Rollouts requiere modificar Istio installation.
options.why: Falso. Argo Rollouts es plug-and-play con Istio installation estándar. Solo requires que Istio esté instalado.

questions.explanation: Setup completo: (1) Deploy Istio (istioctl install); (2) Enable sidecar injection en namespace (label istio-injection=enabled); (3) Crear Service (que apunta a app); (4) Crear DestinationRule con subsets stable/canary; (5) Crear VirtualService con initial routing 100/0; (6) Crear Rollout CRD con trafficRouting.istio + steps. Argo Rollouts controller: watches Rollout, cuando new version detected, crea canary ReplicaSet, updates VirtualService weight gradualmente según steps. Advanced: canary por HEADER (Istio soporta match.headers) para test cohorts específicos antes de weight-based rollout. Envoy: sidecar proxy en cada pod, applies routing rules.
questions.realWorld: Airbnb usa Istio + Argo Rollouts para canary. IBM Cloud Kubernetes Service integrated similar. Adobe similar stack. Argo Rollouts docs tienen full example Istio integration. Flagger integration muy similar (both use Istio APIs).

questions.scenario: Escribiendo AnalysisTemplate reusable para todos los servicios web de tu company. Debe checar success rate y latency, con thresholds tunable per servicio.
questions.question: ¿Cómo diseñar AnalysisTemplates reusables y parameterized?

options.text: Argo Rollouts AnalysisTemplate soporta 'args' — parameters que se pasan al hacer referencia. Ejemplo: template define 'service-name' y 'threshold' como args, query uses {{args.service-name}} y successCondition uses {{args.threshold}}. Rollouts referencian template con args específicos.
options.why: Correcto. Templating permite un solo AnalysisTemplate central compartido por muchos Rollouts, cada uno con sus args. DRY principle.

options.text: ClusterAnalysisTemplate: variant cluster-scoped (vs namespace-scoped). Usar para templates compartidos across namespaces. Platform team define central templates, product teams los referencian.
options.why: Correcto. ClusterAnalysisTemplate es namespace-independent. Governance pattern: platform team owns templates + best practices, product teams focus en business.

options.text: Múltiples metrics en un template: array de metrics, cada uno con su query, successCondition, failureCondition, interval, count. Rollout falla si CUALQUIER metric fails.
options.why: Correcto. Composición AND: success rate > 95% AND p99 < 500ms AND CPU < 80% — todos deben pasar. Provee defense-in-depth analysis.

options.text: Background analysis: paralelo al step progression. Continues durante todos los steps. Rollback inmediato si algo falla en cualquier momento, no solo al final del step.
options.why: Correcto. Rollout.spec.strategy.canary.analysis.templates ejecuta durante entire rollout. Fail = immediate abort. Vs. step-level analysis que solo evalúa entre steps.

options.text: Un AnalysisTemplate por Rollout — no reuse.
options.why: Antipatrón. Duplication = maintenance nightmare. Standardize templates centrally con args.

questions.explanation: AnalysisTemplate structure: metadata.name, spec.args (parameters), spec.metrics (list). Each metric: name, interval (e.g., 30s), count (e.g., 10 checks), successCondition (e.g., 'result[0] >= 0.95'), failureCondition, provider (prometheus/datadog/web/job/kubernetes). Provider prometheus: address + query. Provider web: URL, expects HTTP 200. Provider job: run K8s Job, expects success. Provider kubernetes: check resource state. Composability: Rollout con multiple analysis.templates aggregates results. Templates parametrizadas permite platform team ownership. ClusterAnalysisTemplate = cluster-scoped variant. Best practices: (a) short interval para fast detection; (b) count>1 para tolerate transient spikes; (c) failureLimit para tolerate few failures antes de abort.
questions.realWorld: Intuit tiene central AnalysisTemplate library. Argo docs incluyen many examples. Adobe uses ClusterAnalysisTemplate para governance. GitOps pattern: templates versioned en git repo, deployed via ArgoCD. Flagger equivalent: MetricTemplate CRD.

questions.scenario: Servicio con SLO estricto donde requieres INSTANT cutover (no gradual traffic split). Argo Rollouts soporta blue/green strategy además de canary.
questions.question: ¿Cómo funciona blue/green en Argo Rollouts?

options.text: Rollout.spec.strategy.blueGreen: activeService (production service), previewService (opcional, para testing new version antes de cutover), autoPromotionEnabled (auto-switch después de analysis, o manual), scaleDownDelaySeconds (cuánto tiempo mantener old ReplicaSet running post-cutover para rollback rápido). Al deploy new version: crea nuevo ReplicaSet full-size (100% de replicas), waits ready, runs pre-promotion analysis (opcional), promotes cambiando el Service selector al new ReplicaSet.
options.why: Correcto. Blue/green en Argo Rollouts es más simple que canary — full new deployment ready primero, then instant service selector switch. scaleDownDelaySeconds crítico: mantiene old ReplicaSet durante horas post-cutover para rollback en <segundos (solo switch selector back).

options.text: Requiere DNS-based cutover.
options.why: Falso. Cutover via K8s Service selector switch — instantáneo, no DNS TTL issues.

options.text: Doble el número de replicas siempre y forever.
options.why: Solo temporal — nueva version tiene 100% replicas mientras vieja aún running. Después de scaleDownDelay, vieja se destruye.

options.text: No soporta rollback automatizado.
options.why: Falso. preservation del old ReplicaSet + prePromotionAnalysis permite auto-rollback si analysis falla.

questions.explanation: Blue/green flow Argo Rollouts: (1) apply new Rollout spec (image change); (2) crea nuevo ReplicaSet (green) con full replica count; (3) waits ready + healthy; (4) prePromotionAnalysis runs (opcional): metrics de preview service; (5) si passes, auto-promote (o manual approval); (6) Service selector switches active → new ReplicaSet; (7) postPromotionAnalysis (opcional): confirms new version healthy post-cutover; (8) scaleDownDelay minutes wait; (9) old ReplicaSet scaled down. Ventajas vs canary: (a) simpler mental model; (b) instant cutover, no traffic splitting complexity; (c) trivial rollback (Service selector flip back). Desventajas: (a) doble infra temporal; (b) all-or-nothing (no gradual detection); (c) requires enough cluster capacity.
questions.realWorld: Blue/green common para high-SLO services. Airbnb uses para critical services. Adobe similar. IBM Cloud SDK examples. Trade-off: canary vs blue/green depends on capacity + risk tolerance. Muchas empresas usan ambos: blue/green para high-risk deploys, canary para standard.

questions.topic: Analysis providers — más allá de Prometheus
questions.scenario: Tu company usa Datadog para APM, no Prometheus. Argo Rollouts docs mention 'metric providers'. ¿Puedes hacer analysis con Datadog?
questions.question: ¿Qué metric providers soporta Argo Rollouts?

options.text: Prometheus (native, built-in): queries PromQL, common para Kubernetes ecosystems. Configurable con Prometheus address y query.
options.why: Correcto. Provider más usado. Prometheus + K8s = ecosystem estándar.

options.text: Datadog (built-in): Datadog Query language, API key required. Popular en empresas ya con Datadog para APM.
options.why: Correcto. Argo Rollouts tiene provider Datadog nativo. Similarly Flagger. Muchas empresas usan Datadog para todo — este integration cierra el gap.

options.text: New Relic, Wavefront, CloudWatch, Google Cloud Monitoring: providers built-in adicionales para observability platforms comunes.
options.why: Correcto. Argo Rollouts soporta ecosystem amplio. Cada uno con provider-specific config (address, credentials, query syntax).

options.text: Web provider: HTTP endpoint que retorna JSON. Muy flexible — cualquier system que expose HTTP puede ser metric source. Custom validators.
options.why: Correcto. Extension point para providers no-built-in. Endpoint retorna JSON, jsonPath extrae value, successCondition evalúa. Universal.

options.text: Solo Prometheus está soportado.
options.why: Falso. Ecosystem amplio de providers, más web provider para extensibilidad.

questions.explanation: Argo Rollouts metric providers: (1) Prometheus (address + query PromQL); (2) Datadog (query DD language + API key); (3) New Relic (query + account ID); (4) Wavefront; (5) CloudWatch (query + region + AWS credentials); (6) Graphite; (7) Kubernetes (query resource status); (8) Job (run K8s Job, exit code determines success); (9) Web (HTTP endpoint retorna JSON); (10) Influx. Cada provider en analysisTemplate: metrics[].provider.<providerName>: config. Composable: un template puede usar múltiples providers (Prometheus + CloudWatch + custom Web). Best practice: combinar tech metrics (Prometheus) con business metrics (Datadog o custom endpoint). Flagger soporta similar list.
questions.realWorld: Empresas con Datadog usan Datadog provider. AWS-heavy shops usan CloudWatch. Multi-cloud shops mezclan providers. Custom endpoints comunes para business-specific KPIs (Salesforce data, internal analytics). Adobe, Intuit, Airbnb published sus configurations.

questions.scenario: Rollout stuck en 'Progressing' por 2 horas. Argo Rollouts UI muestra step de analysis fallando. Debug time.
questions.question: ¿Cómo debuggear rollouts stuck o fallando?

options.text: [kubectl argo rollouts get rollout <name>] muestra status detallado: current step, canary replicas, stable replicas, analysis runs status. UI (kubectl argo rollouts dashboard) provee visualización interactiva.
options.why: Correcto. CLI + UI del plugin son primary tools. Muestra step-by-step progression, analysis runs con individual metrics results.

options.text: [kubectl describe analysisrun <name>]: muestra cada metric result, si passed/failed, failureLimit reached, latest measurement value. Central para entender por qué analysis fails.
options.why: Correcto. AnalysisRun es el CRD que representa un analysis instance. describe muestra measurements en detalle.

options.text: Verify metric query in Prometheus UI directamente: si la query no retorna data, o retorna null, analysis falla porque no puede evaluar. Common issue: labels no match (canary label distinto de query filter).
options.why: Correcto. 80% de 'analysis failing' issues son queries malformadas o labels mismatched. Prueba directamente en Prometheus antes de debugging Argo.

options.text: Check that traffic routing está funcionando: [kubectl get virtualservice <name> -o yaml] shows current weights. Si Istio no aplica weights correctamente, canary no recibe traffic → analysis no tiene data.
options.why: Correcto. Muchas veces canary metrics vacías porque canary no recibe traffic (Istio config wrong). Verify weights en VirtualService reflejan step actual.

options.text: Restart Argo Rollouts controller para 'fix' the stuck rollout.
options.why: Antipatrón. Restart controller no fix underlying issue. Debug root cause primero. Restart puede clear stale state pero no fix problems.

questions.explanation: Debugging checklist: (1) [kubectl argo rollouts status <name>]: current step, progress; (2) [kubectl argo rollouts get rollout <name>]: detailed status; (3) [kubectl get analysisrun -n <ns>]: recent analysis runs; (4) [kubectl describe analysisrun <name>]: metric-level results; (5) [kubectl get virtualservice <name> -o yaml]: current traffic weights; (6) Prometheus UI: test queries directly; (7) [kubectl logs -n argo-rollouts <controller-pod>]: controller logs; (8) [kubectl get events]: recent events. Common issues: (a) query malformed; (b) labels mismatch entre canary pods y query filter; (c) traffic no reaching canary (Istio config); (d) metrics no available yet (fresh deploy, no data); (e) failureLimit too strict (transient spikes causing false fail). Argo Rollouts community Slack activo.
questions.realWorld: Intuit, Adobe, Airbnb published debugging playbooks. Argo Rollouts UI (dashboard command) mejora debugging visual. Common story: canary 'failing' porque metric provider address wrong. Diagnostic: run query manual first, then integrate.

questions.scenario: Necesitas exponer nueva version SOLO a internal QA team (con header X-QA-Test: true) antes de rollout público. No weight-based routing.
questions.question: ¿Cómo hacer header-based canary con Argo Rollouts o Flagger?

options.text: Argo Rollouts: canary.trafficRouting.istio.virtualServices con multiple routes en el VirtualService. Route con match.headers.X-QA-Test: exact 'true' → canary subset (weight 100); otra route sin header match → stable (weight 100). Argo Rollouts orchestrates changes progressively. Flagger tiene A/B strategy nativa: canary.analysis.match: [{headers: {x-qa-test: {regex: '^true$'}}}] — orchestrates automatically.
options.why: Correcto. Header-based routing es built-in en Istio VirtualService (o cualquier service mesh). Ambas Argo Rollouts (via Istio integration) y Flagger (via A/B strategy) lo soportan. Uso: internal testing, geo-targeting (via User-Agent), gradual per-user cohort rollout.

options.text: No es posible — Argo Rollouts solo soporta weight-based.
options.why: Falso. Vía Istio/Envoy features, header-based es supported. Requires Istio config en VirtualService.

options.text: Requires custom Envoy filter escrito en Lua.
options.why: Overkill. Istio VirtualService match.headers es declarative sin Lua.

options.text: Solo funciona con AWS ALB.
options.why: Falso. Feature de Istio/Envoy/NGINX/Linkerd. AWS ALB también soporta pero no es único.

questions.explanation: Header-based canary use cases: (1) Internal testing (headers de VPN o QA tools); (2) Geo-targeting (X-Country header from CDN); (3) User cohorts (X-Cohort del auth service); (4) Feature preview (X-Beta-Users). Istio VirtualService: http[0].match: [{headers: {X-QA-Test: {exact: 'true'}}}], route: [{destination: {subset: canary}, weight: 100}]; http[1].route: [{destination: {subset: stable}, weight: 100}]. Order matters en Istio — first match wins. Flagger A/B strategy: canary.analysis.match declarative con headers. Progressive: puedes combinar header-based (internal test) con weight-based (public rollout) en secuencia. Best practice: dogfooding (empleados usan canary primero via header) es zero-risk validation antes de external exposure.
questions.realWorld: Google 'dogfooding' — empleados see internal versions via user headers. Facebook similar. GitHub uses header-based canary para preview features en https://github.com/*/next. Adobe internal QA con VPN-set headers. Weaveworks blog explica patterns.

questions.scenario: Argo Rollouts tiene Experiment CRD (separate from Rollout). Un compañero pregunta: '¿Experiment reemplaza canary? ¿Cuándo usar cada uno?'
questions.question: ¿Qué es Experiment y cómo se diferencia de Canary?

options.text: Experiment CRD es para running EPHEMERAL analysis: temporarily deploy múltiples variants (v1, v2, v3, v4) side-by-side, mide métricas, decide winner. NO deploys a producción — solo comparative analysis. Termina destruyendo todos los variants (o just promoting winner separadamente). Use case: A/B/C testing arquitectura o algorithm variants antes de commit. Canary es progressive rollout que TERMINA en producción; Experiment es temporary evaluation.
options.why: Correcto. Experiment = 'let me run 3 variants at 5% traffic each for 24h, see which performs best'. Canary = 'gradually move all traffic to new version'. Complementarios. Experiment for R&D, Canary for delivery.

options.text: Experiment es sinónimo de Canary.
options.why: Falso. Diferentes CRDs con diferentes purposes.

options.text: Experiment reemplaza Rollout — es la nueva version.
options.why: Falso. Coexisten. Rollout para progressive delivery; Experiment para R&D testing.

options.text: Experiment solo funciona con Google Optimize.
options.why: Falso. Argo Rollouts primitive nativo.

questions.explanation: Experiment CRD spec: duration (e.g., 24h), templates (list of variants a deploy), analysis (metrics para evaluate). Al start: crea Deployments/ReplicaSets per template, envía traffic vía Service mesh, colects metrics durante duration, termina destruyendo variants. Use cases: (1) Algorithm comparison (recommendation v1 vs v2 vs v3); (2) Infra comparison (different node types, different framework versions); (3) Load test comparison. NO reemplaza production traffic — es evaluation temporal. Distinción: Rollout = deployment, Experiment = analysis. Diferencia con full A/B testing tools (Optimizely): Experiment es infra-level (compares versions of the app), A/B testing tools son business-level (compares user behavior con feature variants). Complementarios en stack maduro.
questions.realWorld: Argo Rollouts Experiment usado por Airbnb para infrastructure R&D. Netflix uses similar patterns internally con Spinnaker. Intuit publicó experiencias. Casos típicos: 'A vs B vs C algorithm before deploying winner'.

questions.scenario: Equipo usa Argo CD (GitOps). Quieren añadir progressive delivery. Argo Rollouts es el fit natural. Pero cómo interactúan?
questions.question: ¿Cómo funciona GitOps con Argo Rollouts?

options.text: Rollout CRD vive en git como código (junto con otros manifests). Argo CD detecta cambios en git → aplica al cluster. Al cambiar image tag en git, Argo CD updates el Rollout, Argo Rollouts controller triggers el canary progression.
options.why: Correcto. Rollout es K8s resource declarative como cualquier otro. GitOps flow works cleanly.

options.text: Analysis templates también en git — versionados como config. Central templates en shared repo, referenciados por individual apps. Changes vía PR.
options.why: Correcto. Templates as code. GitOps aplica a todos los CRDs. Best practice para governance.

options.text: Argo CD apps configurables para 'sync only when Rollout is stable'. Argo CD respects Rollout progressing state — no re-syncs while rollout in-flight.
options.why: Correcto. Prevents race conditions donde Argo CD y Argo Rollouts se pelean por el state. Argo CD detects Rollout in progress y waits.

options.text: Rollback via git: revert commit en git, Argo CD detects, applies revert, Argo Rollouts triggers new rollout (con new-old version). Audit trail complete en git.
options.why: Correcto. GitOps + Rollouts = full auditability. Rollback es git operation. Nada aplicado outside git.

options.text: Argo Rollouts bypasses git — cambios se hacen directamente en cluster.
options.why: Antipatrón GitOps. Todo debe pasar por git. Direct cluster changes crean drift.

questions.explanation: GitOps + Argo Rollouts flow: (1) developer merges PR con new image tag en Rollout manifest; (2) Argo CD detects git change; (3) Argo CD applies Rollout update to cluster; (4) Argo Rollouts controller detects Rollout spec change; (5) starts canary progression (steps + analysis); (6) durante progression, Argo Rollouts modifies live objects (VirtualService weights, ReplicaSets) — NO writes back to git; (7) if success, promotion completes; (8) if fail, rollback (Argo Rollouts state, no git change). Nota crítico: Argo CD debe ser configurado con syncPolicy que respect Rollout state — usually con 'ignoreDifferences' para status fields o annotations. Anti-patrón: Argo CD tries to sync while Rollout progressing → conflict → issues. Solution: configure Argo CD app con proper resource hooks.
questions.realWorld: Intuit (originators of Argo) uses este stack. Adobe similar. IBM Cloud. Many published GitOps + Progressive Delivery patterns. Argo Rollouts docs incluyen best practices para GitOps integration.

questions.scenario: Team maduro con SLOs definidos (99.9% availability, p99 < 500ms). Quieren tie canary analysis a SLO burn rate — si canary burns budget muy rápido, abort.
questions.question: ¿Cómo integrar SLO burn rate en canary analysis?

options.text: SLO burn rate query en Prometheus: multi-window multi-burn rate (Google SRE Workbook). Ejemplo: (1 - success_rate_5m) / (1 - SLO_target) — si canary burn rate > 14.4x en 1h window = fast burn = abort canary immediately.
options.why: Correcto. Google SRE Workbook Ch. 5 explica multi-window burn rate. Combinamos: fast burn (14.4x en 1h) + slow burn (6x en 6h) = comprehensive coverage. Applied to canary metrics.

options.text: Custom Prometheus recording rules para SLO calculation. Preescritas queries para success rate por servicio con SLO metadata. Analysis template reference recording rules. Consistency across services.
options.why: Correcto. Recording rules pre-compute expensive queries. Servicios reference standard rules. Governance central.

options.text: Google 'SLO Generator' tool o Sloth (OSS) generan Prometheus rules from SLO definitions. Declarative SLO config → auto-generated recording+alerting rules. Includes burn rate calculations.
options.why: Correcto. Sloth (OSS por Xabier Larrakoetxea) genera Prometheus rules from YAML SLO config. Integrable con Argo Rollouts analysisTemplate para consistent SLO-based analysis across services.

options.text: Trade-off: canary de N minutos vs SLO measurement window. Canary too short = poor SLO signal. Ajustar canary steps + analysis intervals para have enough data. SLO measurement generalmente rolling 28-30 días, pero canary usa short windows (5-60min) que aproximan.
options.why: Correcto. Statistical significance issue. Canary de 10 min con 100 requests/min = 1000 data points — enough para 99.9% SLO analysis (needs to see if error rate is 0.1% approx). Low-traffic services need longer windows.

options.text: SLO burn rate no aplica a canary — solo a alerting.
options.why: Falso. SLO burn rate se aplica a cualquier scenario donde quieres tie decisions to SLO impact. Canary abort si burn budget rápido = perfectly valid.

questions.explanation: SLO-based canary analysis: (1) define SLO (99.9% availability); (2) define burn rate thresholds (fast: 14.4x in 1h, slow: 6x in 6h, per Google SRE); (3) Prometheus recording rules calculate current burn rate; (4) analysisTemplate query burn rate para canary window; (5) successCondition: burn_rate < threshold. Tools: Sloth (declarative SLO → Prometheus rules), Pyrra (similar), OpenSLO (spec + tooling), Nobl9 (SaaS). Argo Rollouts + Sloth pattern: define SLO en Sloth YAML, apply to cluster, referenceable in Rollout AnalysisTemplate. Ventajas SLO-based vs raw thresholds: (a) meaningful (aligned with user experience); (b) budget concept forces thinking about acceptable risk; (c) uniform across services (all use same framework). Gotchas: (a) low-traffic services no tienen enough data para tight SLOs; (b) canary window > SLO window can be confusing.
questions.realWorld: Google internal uses SLO-driven canary. Sloth (OSS) publicado 2020 por Xabier at Spotify. Many teams have adopted. Nobl9 SaaS. LinkedIn published extensively sobre SLO + progressive delivery. Blueprint pattern maduro pero requires solid SLO practice primero.

questions.scenario: Deployment a 20 clusters (múltiples regions, edge, dev/staging/prod). Coordinar progressive delivery across clusters es complejo.
questions.question: ¿Cómo escalar progressive delivery multi-cluster?

options.text: Argo CD ApplicationSet: generate múltiples Applications from template (per-cluster). Central ApplicationSet controls what deploys where. Progressive por cluster: staging → dev → prod-region-1 → prod-region-2. Each cluster runs its own Argo Rollouts canary.
options.why: Correcto. ApplicationSet es el escalable pattern. Central declarative config, dispatched to N clusters. Each cluster independently progresses.

options.text: Waves: Argo CD sync waves (order of application). Progressive delivery entre clusters (region 1 first, wait 24h, region 2, etc.) enforced by wave numbers.
options.why: Correcto. sync-wave annotations control order. Combined con analysis at each wave = multi-cluster progressive delivery.

options.text: External orchestration (Spinnaker, custom): orquesta despliegues cross-cluster con analysis en cada cluster + global decisions. Spinnaker fue diseñado para multi-cloud/multi-region deployment orchestration.
options.why: Correcto. Spinnaker (Netflix originalmente) diseñado para multi-cluster/region orchestration. Más maduro que Argo para multi-cloud scenarios. Alternative: custom orchestration con GitHub Actions + kubectl.

options.text: Regional canary: primero canary en region small (5% traffic), if OK, canary en region grande. Coordination via metrics (both regions monitored) o via successive git commits (approve region 1, then region 2).
options.why: Correcto. Regional deploy waves. Combine con per-region canary = nested gradualness. Amazon pattern.

options.text: Deploy simultaneous a todos los clusters para consistency.
options.why: Antipatrón. Simultaneous = no blast radius contain. Waves preferido.

questions.explanation: Multi-cluster progressive delivery patterns: (1) Argo CD ApplicationSet con progressive sync (dev → staging → prod-r1 → prod-r2); (2) Sync waves para intra-cluster ordering; (3) Argo Rollouts en cada cluster para intra-cluster canary; (4) External orchestrator (Spinnaker, custom) para complex flows. Coordination challenges: (a) different clusters may have different SLOs; (b) region-specific metrics (canary metrics must be regional); (c) rollback coordination (rollback en cluster N should abort clusters N+1, N+2); (d) feature flags para consistency user-facing. Spinnaker approach: pipelines declarative, per-region canaries, global rollback triggers. Argo approach: GitOps-native, PR-based rollout of git branches per environment. Tradeoffs: Argo = simpler, GitOps-native; Spinnaker = more complex, more powerful for multi-cluster.
questions.realWorld: Netflix Spinnaker deploys across AWS regions. Google Cloud Deploy multi-region. Argo team publishing multi-cluster patterns. IBM, Adobe uses ApplicationSet pattern. Cloudflare deploys across 300+ PoPs con custom orchestration.

questions.scenario: Rollouts pasan pero después de 6h en producción se descubre latency regression subtle. Analysis solo corrió durante canary steps (2h max). Cómo detectar issues post-promotion?
questions.question: ¿Cómo implementar continuous analysis post-promotion?

options.text: Argo Rollouts postPromotionAnalysis: analysis que corre AFTER promotion completes. Ejecuta durante ventana (hours-days) checking metrics vs pre-deploy baseline. Failure = manual investigation (no auto-rollback typically because promotion already done).
options.why: Correcto. postPromotionAnalysis extension del canary primitive. Runs analysis post-cutover para detect delayed regressions. Cannot auto-rollback (state committed) pero alerta para human intervention.

options.text: SLO burn rate alerts continuous (24/7): if service consistently burning budget faster post-deploy, alert on-call. Not tied to Rollout — general observability. Detects delayed regressions independent of deployment tool.
options.why: Correcto. SLO alerts as continuous monitoring. Independent from Rollout state. Google SRE Workbook alerting on burn rate.

options.text: Chaos engineering post-deploy: automated experiments post-promotion (kill pods, inject latency) to verify new version handles failure modes correctly. Chaos Toolkit, LitmusChaos.
options.why: Correcto. Chaos post-deploy validates resilience — algo que canary metrics (con normal traffic) no captures. LinkedIn Waterbear pattern.

options.text: Automatic performance regression detection: baseline p99 pre-deploy vs post-deploy across días. Statistical significance test. Alert cuando new version's p99 consistently peor.
options.why: Correcto. Delayed regressions (memory leaks, DB connection exhaustion) manifest en días. Continuous comparison detects them.

options.text: Analysis termina en promotion — no necesidad de más monitoring.
options.why: Antipatrón. Regressions happen post-deploy — continuous monitoring esencial.

questions.explanation: Post-promotion analysis patterns: (1) postPromotionAnalysis en Argo Rollouts — declarative time-bound analysis; (2) SLO burn rate alerting (continuous, on-call notification); (3) Performance regression detection (statistical tests across días); (4) Chaos engineering (verify resilience of new version); (5) Business metrics monitoring (revenue, conversion). Framework: layered observability. Canary analysis catches immediate bugs; post-promotion catches delayed. Together = defense in depth. Herramientas: Argo Rollouts postPromotionAnalysis + Sloth/Nobl9 SLO alerts + LitmusChaos + custom performance dashboards. Cadence: canary analysis (minutes); postPromotionAnalysis (hours-days); continuous SLO monitoring (forever). Anti-patterns: 'canary passed, deploy successful' = incomplete. 'Successful deploy = successful production for the next month' = wrong framing.
questions.realWorld: Netflix combines canary + post-deploy analysis con Kayenta + Atlas metrics. Google internal similar patterns. Facebook post-launch monitoring. Airbnb SLO-driven observability. Adobe published patterns con Argo Rollouts + Datadog SLO tracking.

questions.topic: Comparison — Argo Rollouts vs Flagger vs Spinnaker
questions.scenario: CTO pregunta '¿cuál progressive delivery tool adoptamos?' Necesitas comparar objetivamente Argo Rollouts, Flagger, y Spinnaker.
questions.question: ¿Cuáles son los tradeoffs principales entre estos tools?

options.text: Argo Rollouts: K8s-native (CRDs), lightweight, integra con Argo CD (GitOps), moderate learning curve, extensive metric providers, ampla community, active development. Best fit: K8s environments con Argo CD, teams que valoran declarativa/GitOps.
options.why: Correcto. Argo Rollouts es el más adoptado en pure K8s environments. Ownership Intuit-originated ahora CNCF Incubating.

options.text: Flagger: K8s-native, más opinionated (simpler config), tight integration con Flux, extensive metric providers, mesh-native (Istio, Linkerd, App Mesh, NGINX, etc.). Best fit: Flux-based GitOps stacks, teams que quieren minimal config.
options.why: Correcto. Flagger's opinionated approach means less flexibility pero less complexity. Weaveworks + Flux + Flagger es coherent stack.

options.text: Spinnaker: multi-cloud (not K8s-only), maduro (Netflix-originated 2015), complex to operate (JVM services), extensive multi-region orchestration, integrates con Kayenta para statistical analysis. Best fit: multi-cloud environments, complex deployment orchestration, teams con dedicated deployment infra ops.
options.why: Correcto. Spinnaker más maduro pero más costoso operacionalmente. Vale la pena para multi-cloud complex scenarios. K8s-only teams típicamente prefer Argo Rollouts o Flagger por simplicidad.

options.text: Ninguno es 'mejor' universalmente — decision depends on: (1) K8s-only vs multi-cloud; (2) GitOps tool ya adoptado (Argo CD vs Flux); (3) team ownership del deployment infra; (4) complexity tolerance.
options.why: Correcto. Decision framework contextual. Same team con Flux + Weaveworks stack pick Flagger; team con Argo CD + K8s only pick Argo Rollouts; team con AWS + GCP + on-prem may need Spinnaker.

options.text: Todos son idénticos — solo nombres distintos.
options.why: Falso. Real differences en architecture, integration, complexity, feature set.

questions.explanation: Comparison matrix: | Feature | Argo Rollouts | Flagger | Spinnaker |. K8s-native: Yes/Yes/Uses K8s but broader. GitOps: Argo CD tight/Flux tight/Any (agnostic). Traffic split: mesh+ingress/mesh+ingress/mesh+LB. Analysis: templates+providers/metricTemplates+providers/Kayenta+providers. Multi-cloud: K8s-based/K8s-based/Native multi-cloud. Complexity: Moderate/Low/High. Community: Large (Argo family)/Moderate/Large (mature). Selection guide: (1) K8s + Argo CD → Argo Rollouts; (2) K8s + Flux → Flagger; (3) Multi-cloud, complex → Spinnaker; (4) Just K8s, simple, minimal deps → Flagger o Argo Rollouts. Migration paths: Spinnaker → Argo Rollouts common; rarely reverse.
questions.realWorld: Netflix runs Spinnaker (created it). Intuit runs Argo Rollouts (created it). Weaveworks runs Flagger (created it). Vendor bias natural. IBM Cloud + Adobe use Argo Rollouts. Trend Micro uses Flagger. Airbnb hybrid. Google Cloud Deploy has similar concepts.

questions.scenario: Después de 6 meses con Argo Rollouts, tu team observa: canaries que 'siempre pasan' (thresholds tan loose que nada falla), rollouts stuck, incidents que canary no detectó.
questions.question: ¿Cuáles son los failure modes comunes de progressive delivery?

options.text: Loose thresholds ('canary theater'): thresholds tan permisivos (success rate > 50%) que canary nunca fails. Falso sense of security. Fix: baseline-comparative (canary vs stable en tiempo real), no absolute thresholds. Kayenta approach.
options.why: Correcto. Common failure. Team pone thresholds loose para evitar false positives, pero pierde detection real. Kayenta baseline-comparative es antidote.

options.text: Low-traffic services: no enough requests para statistical significance en canary window. Analysis fails or passes basado en noise. Fix: extended windows, sampling of real users a canary via feature flags, o skip canary para low-traffic (rely on rolling update).
options.why: Correcto. Real issue. Canary a 1% de 10 req/s = 0.1 req/s = 6 req/min. Not enough. Solutions: extend window, sample users, or acknowledge canary limitation.

options.text: Metric provider outage: si Prometheus down, analysis can't run. Rollout stuck o fail-open (proceed) o fail-closed (rollback). Fix: fail-open with alerting typically (don't block deploys si observability fails), plus reliable metric provider.
options.why: Correcto. Fragility de dependency. Prometheus outage shouldn't block deployment. Argo Rollouts default is fail-closed; may want to configure fail-open.

options.text: Long-tail bugs: canary de 30 min no detects issues que aparecen after hours (memory leaks, connection pool exhaustion). postPromotionAnalysis + continuous SLO monitoring catch these.
options.why: Correcto. Time window limitation. Solution: complementary continuous monitoring post-promotion.

options.text: Progressive delivery elimina TODOS los failure modes.
options.why: Antipatrón overconfidence. PD reduces risk but doesn't eliminate. Complementary practices needed.

questions.explanation: Common failure modes: (1) Canary theater (loose thresholds, no real detection); (2) Insufficient traffic (statistical power problem); (3) Metric provider dependency; (4) Long-tail bugs (short canary window misses); (5) Regional bugs (canary en region A pero bug specific region B); (6) User-specific bugs (canary users are internal, users are external); (7) State-dependent bugs (bug only reveals con production data patterns); (8) Timing bugs (bug appears only in specific hours). Mitigations: (a) baseline-comparative analysis (Kayenta); (b) SLO burn rate integration; (c) postPromotionAnalysis extended windows; (d) chaos engineering; (e) traffic sampling (real users a canary); (f) feature flags para instant rollback; (g) continuous observability posDeploy. Progressive delivery = powerful but not silver bullet. Combining con feature flags + observability + chaos + rollback drills = comprehensive safety net.
questions.realWorld: Etsy, Netflix, Google published post-mortems donde canary passed but production had issues. Common learning: canary is necessary not sufficient. Complementary layers needed. Argo Rollouts community shares failure patterns.

questions.topic: Adoption journey — de rolling a progressive delivery
questions.scenario: Team con K8s + rolling updates. CTO quiere progressive delivery. ¿Cómo la adoption journey realistic?
questions.question: ¿Cómo estructurar la adopción de progressive delivery?

options.text: Phase 1 (weeks): observability foundation. Deploy Prometheus + Grafana + alerts. Define SLIs per servicio. Sin observability, canary analysis no puede funcionar. Verify metrics correctly instrumented, dashboards understand.
options.why: Correcto. Observability es prerequisite. Puedes hacer canary sin Prometheus pero no analysis automatizado.

options.text: Phase 2 (weeks): pilot service. Elige un service (ideally not critical, high enough traffic para statistical significance). Install Argo Rollouts o Flagger. Configure canary con manual approvals (no auto-promotion). Team learns primitives.
options.why: Correcto. Start small. Manual gates initially. Team learns Rollout, AnalysisTemplate, VirtualService, debugging.

options.text: Phase 3 (months): analysis automation. Introduce automated analysis (Prometheus queries). Start conservative (loose thresholds). Iterate para tighten thresholds based on observed variability. Track false positive/negative rates.
options.why: Correcto. Analysis maturity is journey. Start loose, learn baselines, tighten. Requires patience.

options.text: Phase 4 (months): expand + governance. Roll out a más servicios. Platform team owns Templates centralmente. Product teams reference templates + provide app-specific args. Governance via GitOps + PR review.
options.why: Correcto. Scaling requires governance. Central templates, decentralized adoption. Platform engineering pattern.

options.text: Deploy Argo Rollouts en todos los services el primer día.
options.why: Antipatrón. Big bang = disaster. Team no entiende yet, incidents blame progressive delivery, adoption fails.

questions.explanation: Adoption phases realistic: (1) Observability foundation (Prometheus + SLIs); (2) Pilot service con manual canary; (3) Automated analysis con conservative thresholds; (4) Expansion a más services con central Templates; (5) SLO integration (Sloth, burn rate); (6) postPromotionAnalysis y chaos. Timeline: 6-12 months para full adoption typical. Prerequisites: (a) K8s environment; (b) service mesh o Ingress with weighted routing; (c) metrics infrastructure (Prometheus most common); (d) team willing to learn; (e) leadership buy-in. Common pitfalls: (a) skipping observability foundation; (b) big bang adoption; (c) tight thresholds early (false positives); (d) no post-adoption learning (canary theater sets in). Success indicators: (a) deploy frequency increases; (b) change failure rate decreases; (c) MTTR decreases; (d) team confidence up.
questions.realWorld: Intuit, Adobe published adoption journeys. Intuit's Argo team documents the journey extensively. Adobe similar. Learning: progressive delivery is journey, not switch. Cultural + technical + operational. Best fit: teams already doing solid CI/CD, K8s, observability.
